Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (M/M59/M59n1540.xml). General Discourses of Chan Master Dahui Pujue. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB383.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanxiu. Hanxiu Ruqian owns the retained deployment: at the Upper-Lantern close, the sacred work done, opens the sack: go east and west as you please — only carry the bite that kills pig and dog, meet him and bite him dead, and do not fear the knife or shy from the arrow.

Senses.Explanation: The stride of the leaving: retreat done, gold wind in the leaves, the brothers go east and west. Dongshan's stock line sends them to where not an inch of grass grows in ten thousand li, Shishuang answers that out the gate is grass — and every generation warns the leaver what waits on the road. The source case and its second head: Dahui Zonggao retells Dongshan's summer-end address — early autumn, summer's end, brothers going east and west, go straight to where for ten thousand li not an inch of grass grows — and rules that once the saying was out no answer met Dongshan's intent, till a monk carried it to Shishuang, who said only: why not say, out the gate is grass; Guantao Daqi quotes the same retreat-ending address, holds the long silence, then asks how one goes at the no-grass place — and looks left and right before giving it. The stride in live mouths: Yinyuan Longqi has what bursts out of the Huangbo mountains past knotted brows and touching nostrils — no net will hold it, no call turns its head: seven passages open, going east and west, across and athwart without hindrance, free to kill and free to give life, with the one road of turning the body still to be known; Tian'an Sheng denies the assembly ever took one word of his teaching — tomorrow the furnace ends, going east and west, and in days to come do not say Dajue did nothing for you; Feiyin Tongrong unties the labor-stiffened sweat-shirts for the cool breeze — good to go east and west, come south and go north, free and easy — then asks what they will do when a fierce tiger sits square in the road ahead; Baichi Xingyuan prices the walker at eight dou of gold a day, then — nine summers' work done, gold wind stirring the leaves — sends them east and west to meet Widow Ling grabbing the chest, glue forbidden in the mouth; Chaozong Tongren, asked how the patch-robed are forged once the retreat ends, answers: let them go east and west, one and all — what the cage cannot hold must break through the cage, what wrapping cannot wrap is first to open the wrapping; Hanxiu Ruqian at the Upper-Lantern close, the sacred work done, opens the sack: go east and west as you please — only carry the bite that kills pig and dog, meet him and bite him dead, and do not fear the knife or shy from the arrow.
